title: Vegetables Highest in Potassium

seo.title: Vegetables Highest in Potassium per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Beet greens, spinach, Swiss chard, and Brussels sprouts are good sources. Beet greens can exceed 700 mg/100 g and spinach is around 560 mg.
seo.search_intent: Compare potassium-rich vegetables with numbers per 100 grams and serving context.

excerpt: Among leafy vegetables, beet greens stand out at more than 700 mg potassium per 100 g in common databases; spinach is around 560 mg, Swiss chard around 380 mg, and Brussels sprouts near 390 mg. Serving size and cooking method change the amount you actually eat.
content_html:
Bananas get most of the potassium publicity, but several vegetables contain as much or more potassium per 100 g.

Some concentrated vegetable sources

Raw vegetableApprox. potassium/100 g
Beet greens~760 mg
Spinach~560 mg
Brussels sprouts~390 mg
Swiss chard~380 mg
Broccoli~315 mg

Values are rounded and vary with cultivar and preparation.

Cooking can push the numbers in opposite directions

Losing water can concentrate minerals per 100 g, while boiling in a large amount of water can leach potassium into the cooking liquid. If that liquid is discarded, the final amount eaten can be lower.

Serving size matters

One hundred grams of raw spinach is a very large bowl, while 100 g cooked is compact. A 6-ounce serving of broccoli may contribute more total potassium than a small handful of a higher-ranking leafy green.

Not everyone should deliberately increase potassium

For most people, potassium-rich foods are encouraged. People with certain kidney diseases or medications may need individualized limits.

Potassium is not just a fruit nutrient; leafy greens and cruciferous vegetables can contribute heavily to daily intake.

faq.question: Does spinach have more potassium than banana?
faq.answer: Per 100 g, raw spinach is around 560 mg while banana is around 350–360 mg, although typical serving sizes differ.

faq.question: Does boiling lower potassium?
faq.answer: It can if potassium leaches into the cooking water and that water is discarded.

faq.question: Should everyone seek more potassium?
faq.answer: No. Some people with kidney disease or certain medications need to limit potassium under medical guidance.
